origins: Many of us learned this from a boss who underpaid us, a landlord who ignored repairs, a family who felt looked down on, or a community that felt used. Stories and media can add to it. Real unfairness exists, so the belief grows from something true. But when it becomes a rule about every wealthy person, it can block friendships, jobs, mentors, and even our own ability to prosper without guilt.
teaches: Scripture warns about the dangers of riches and the injustice of those who oppress the poor. It also tells us that the rich and the poor have this in common: the Lord is Maker of them all. Job was blameless and upright and was also very wealthy. Zacchaeus, a rich man, gave half his possessions to the poor and was welcomed by Jesus. James says not to show favoritism, and Paul tells the rich to be generous and ready to share. Trust is measured by character, not by bank balance.
self_statements: Rich people got there by cheating.
They look down on people like me.
They will always put money first.
I cannot be friends with someone who has that much.
If I become wealthy, I will become like them.
errors: Treating every wealthy person as the same.
Turning a few hurtful experiences into a rule.
Assuming that I know what a wealthy person thinks of me.
Believing that people are either poor and good or rich and bad.
questions: Whom did I learn this from, and what actually happened?
Do I know any wealthy people who are honest and kind? What do I know about them?
Do I know any poor people who have been unfair or unkind? What does that show?
What does Scripture say about how to judge a person?
How does this belief affect my opportunities or my own view of success?
What would it look like to treat people as individuals?
truth: Some wealthy people have wronged others, and so have some poor people. Wealth does not decide whether a person is trustworthy. God made us all, and He looks at character and the heart. I can be wise, set boundaries where needed, and still treat each person as an individual.
hw_truths: The rich and the poor are both made by God.
Character matters more than a bank balance.
I can be wise without stereotyping.
I can prosper and stay generous.
I can judge people one at a time.
log: Each week, note one person who did not fit a stereotype you held, and what you saw.
actions: Write down what happened to you or your family and what you learned.
Learn about a wealthy person known for integrity and generosity.
Next time you meet someone, notice their actions before you assign a category.
Write what generous, trustworthy success would look like for you.
prayer: Lord, You are Maker of the rich and the poor. Heal what has been done to me and my family, and keep me from judging others by their bank balance. Give me wisdom to see character and a heart that stays generous. Amen.
hw_questions: Who does not fit this belief?
What does Scripture say about judging people?
How does this belief affect me?
How can I judge people one at a time?
name_example: Sarah can write: “God made the rich and the poor, so I can look at character, not just a bank balance.”
